## Trip highlights

The first few days introduce you to the coffee, volcanic landscapes and tropical forests of central and northern Costa Rica. At the Doka plantation, you’ll see the entire coffee production process before heading to the Poás crater and La Paz waterfalls.

The focus then shifts to wildlife. In Caño Negro, you’ll take a boat trip along the Río Frío. Around Arenal, explore the forest from the Mistico hanging bridges and the Ecoglide zip lines, and see the old lava fields from the 1968 eruption.

On the way to Manuel Antonio, take a two-hour boat trip on the Tárcoles River, where you may spot large American crocodiles and birds. The route then reaches the Pacific coast, with Manuel Antonio National Park, beaches and forest, and a final marine outing around Bahía Ballena.

## How the route unfolds

The first four days take you into the mountains and the tropical north. The route links a coffee farm, an active volcanic landscape, waterfalls and rainforest with a boat trip through a nature reserve. Around Arenal, there are three ways to experience the forest: on foot, from hanging bridges and by zip line above the trees.

The second half of the trip gradually moves towards the Pacific. A boat trip on the Tárcoles breaks up the drive to Manuel Antonio, and the following days take in beaches, mangroves and marine wildlife. Over eight days, the journey takes you from coffee farms and volcanoes to places where you can see crocodiles, monkeys, tropical birds and dolphins, with a chance of seeing whales in season.
